question: In triangle ABC , BD perp AC at D and angle DBC = 71^circ . E is a point on BC such that angle CAE = 55^circ . What is the measure of angle AEB ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled ΔBDC, the sum of the acute angles is 90°.

⇒ ∠C = 90° − ∠DBC = 90° − 71° = 19°

By the Exterior Angle Theorem in ΔAEC, the exterior angle at E is equal to the sum of the opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 55° + 19° = 74°

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ BD ⊥ AC, so ∠BDC = 90°

⇒ ∠DBC = 71°

⇒ ∠CAE = 55°

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔBDC, the sum of all interior angles is strictly 180°.

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (∠BDC + ∠DBC)

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (90° + 71°) = 19°

⇒ Considering ΔAEC, points B, E, and C are collinear, meaning ∠AEB directly acts as the exterior angle to ΔAEC.

⇒ By the exterior angle theorem, the exterior angle equals the exact sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠ACE

⇒ ∠AEB = 55° + 19°

⇒ ∠AEB = 74°

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a Euclidean triangle is strictly 180°.

Right-Angled Triangle Rules

In a right triangle, one angle is exactly 90°, making the other two acute angles complementary (sum = 90°).
